abstract: DNA-protein crosslinks (DPCs) are complex lesions that block replication, transcription, and other DNA transactions. Here we investigate repair of 3 DPC lesions using the site-specific Flp tyrosine recombinase H305L mutant that forms stable covalent complexes. In human cells, removal or catalytic inhibition of MRE11 stabilizes Flp DPCs in parallel to a proteasome-dependent pathway. High levels of Flp DPCs are also observed in budding yeast, where MRE11 deletion or mutation of the nuclease domain increases covalent Flp DPC accumulation. Mass spectrometry-based identification of endogenous DPC factors in human cells identifies TOP1 covalent complexes as the primary 3 lesion that is stabilized in the absence of MRE11 nuclease function, in addition to 5 DPCs generated by TOP2 family enzymes. This work characterizes an important role for the MRE11-RAD50-NBS1 complex in processing of 3 lesions, in addition to its well-established functions at 5 DPCs and in 5 strand resection during homologous recombination.
